name: Beef Manhattan Bowls
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Verified at 468 cal / 44g protein for beef and gravy alone at 6 servings; the dish is defined as being served over mashed potatoes, which pushes it near 700 cal at 46g protein. Midwest diner classic, extremely cheap, and the catalog has nothing in the open-faced-roast-beef lane. Confidence: high. | HARVEST: Source states nutrition is for the beef and gravy only, excluding the bread and mashed potatoes. Last three lines are under a 'FOR SERVING' header.
intro_html: A Beef Manhattan is a Midwest diner plate: shredded roast beef and brown gravy spooned over mashed potatoes, no ceremony, no garnish. It shows up on lunch counters from Indiana to Nebraska and it has kept people fed cheaply for seventy years. We build it in a slow cooker and portion it into bowls. Each bowl carries 48 grams of protein and 581 calories for about $5.78 (at everyday cost).
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Brown Gravy Mix, 2.25 oz: ~$1.24. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 3 0.87oz packets.
Onion Soup Mix, 2.25 oz: ~$2.11. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 2.2oz 2ct boxes.
Red Wine Vinegar, 0.5 cups: ~$0.84. Buy 1 (lasts several batches).
Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper): ~$0.17. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $62.79 across 14 servings, so roughly $4.49 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $63.31 across 14 servings, roughly $4.52 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $17.68 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $80.99. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $5.78 a bowl (at everyday cost). Six ingredients, one of them potatoes, and the gravy comes out of two packets that cost less than a cup of coffee.
shop_smart: Brown gravy mix and onion soup mix both come in multi packet boxes. The per packet price is lower and they sit in the pantry for a year without complaint.
Russet potatoes mash better than waxy ones and cost less per pound. Buy the big bag and use the extras for the other potato recipes in this section.
Chuck roast is what a Manhattan is supposed to be made of. This is one of the rare cases where the cheap answer is also the traditional one.
Red wine vinegar is a long life pantry bottle. A little goes in here to cut the salt from the two seasoning packets, so do not skip it.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Pat the chuck roast dry, season it with salt and black pepper, and sear it in the olive oil until it is browned on every side.
Set the roast in the slow cooker and sprinkle the brown gravy mix and onion soup mix over the top.
Add the red wine vinegar and enough water to come about a third of the way up the roast.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, until the beef shreds with no effort.
About 40 minutes before you portion, peel and boil the potatoes until a knife slides through, then drain and mash them with some of the hot gravy from the cooker.
Shred the beef in the cooker and stir it through the gravy so nothing dries out.
Taste the gravy. Two seasoning packets bring plenty of salt, so it likely needs pepper rather than more salt.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Spread that weight of mashed potatoes into each container first, then spoon an even weight of shredded beef and gravy over the top. Each bowl lands at 581 calories with 48 grams of protein.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from themagicalslowcooker.com, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
upsell_html: Diner style beef and gravy for about $5.78 a bowl (at everyday cost). This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: Beef Manhattan bowls meal prep: slow cooked shredded chuck roast in brown gravy spooned over mashed potatoes, Midwest diner style. 581 calories, 48g protein, about $5.78 per serving (at everyday cost).
head.keywords: beef manhattan, open faced roast beef, shredded beef and gravy, mashed potato bowls, budget meal prep, midwest diner recipes
steps: Sear the seasoned chuck roast in olive oil until browned all over.
Set it in the slow cooker with brown gravy mix, onion soup mix, vinegar, and water.
Cook on low 8 hours until the beef shreds easily.
Boil and mash the potatoes with some of the hot gravy.
Shred the beef into the gravy and portion over the potatoes into 14 containers.
